title: Compute4Biology: Taking Stock of High Performance Computing Needs for Foundation Models in Biological Sciences
problem: Foundation models are transforming biological sciences, but their computational needs are highly diverse across domains (genomics, proteomics, chemistry). There is no systematic understanding of HPC requirements or co-design principles for biological AI workloads.
motivation: AI-driven discovery in biology is accelerating, but HPC infrastructure is often designed for generic ML workloads. Biological domains have unique computational bottlenecks (I/O, memory, specialized kernels) that require tailored system design.
method: Systematic cross-domain analysis of foundation models in genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, chemistry, and biomedical literature. Characterizes computational bottlenecks, I/O patterns, memory requirements, and compute kernels for each domain.
key_novelty: First systematic cross-domain analysis of HPC needs for biological foundation models; domain-specific characterization of bottlenecks; unified set of HPC co-design principles.
contributions: First systematic cross-domain HPC characterization for biological foundation models
Domain-specific analysis: genomics I/O demands, protein structure memory pressure, molecular modeling kernels
Identification of common patterns and trade-offs in hardware utilization
Data management and software stack design principles
Best practices and co-design principles for next-generation HPC systems
limitations: Rapidly evolving foundation models; heterogeneous domain requirements; trade-offs between domains; cost of specialized hardware.
